To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oxidation-reduction reactions of the Q-cycle enzymes are in agreement with a Q-cycle model in which the quinone-binding sites of the two domains of the enzymes do not exchange electrons with each other on a timescale of milliseconds.

the oxidation of cytochromeb in initially fully reduced mitochondria is not a simple first-order reaction and the oxidation-reduction reaction of cytochrome c + c1 in fully reduced mitochondria does not show a simple first-order dependence on cytochrome c.
the kinetics of oxidation-reduction of cytochrome c1, cytochrome b and cytochrome c in initially fully-reduced mitochondrial membranes are in full agreement with the Q cycle hypothesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the respiratory chain in mitochondria.
the kinetics of electron transport in the respiratory chain.
the elucidation of the mechanism of the QH2-cytochrome c oxidase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Q-cycle is supported by our results and the SQ-cycle is not.
the Q-cycle hypothesis is the best model to explain the kinetics of the electron transfer reactions in mitochondrial membranes.
the Q-cycle hypothesis, but not the SQ-cycle, is consistent with the data obtained in the present study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Q-cycle mechanism, in which the quinone-binding sites of the enzyme are not in direct contact, is the mechanism that is operating in the mitochondrial QH2: cytochrome c oxidase.

the Q-cycle is the preferred mechanism for cytochrome bc1 complexes and the QH2:fumarate oxidoreductase from the bacterium Wolinella succinogenes, whereas the SQ-cycle mechanism is preferred for the cytochrome b6f complex.

the oxidation-reduction behaviour of the QH2-cytochrome c oxidase system is consistent with the Q-cycle mechanism, but that the presence of semiquinones cannot be excluded on the basis of these experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Q-cycle is a robust mechanism for electron transfer in mitochondrial QH2: cytochrome c oxidase.
